findings.issue_text: [P1] src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — The registered `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` now points to an abstract `StatefulDetectorHandler` subclass with none of the required state-extraction or occurrence-construction methods, so every metric-alert detector loses its previously instantiable handler and cannot participate in the detector pipeline.

tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:190 — [75/P2] `detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH` supplies 6 for a packet whose `group_2` value is 10, while the helper discards `value`, so verification cannot detect a hook that builds every group’s occurrence from the wrong evaluated value.

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — P1: `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass` leaves every newly required abstract stateful method unimplemented, so processing any existing `metric_alert_fire` detector now raises `TypeError` while instantiating its handler instead of preserving the prior no-op transition behavior.

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — P1 confidence 100 verbatim `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`: processing a detector of registered type `metric_alert_fire` instantiates this class through `Detector.detector_handler` and raises `TypeError` because it implements none of the now-abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or `build_occurrence_and_event_data` methods.

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — Every `metric_alert_fire` detector now fails with `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` because `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):\n    pass` inherits the unimplemented abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` methods, so `detector_handler` cannot be created and no packet is processed.

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — P1 [anchor:100] Replacing the working placeholder with `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass` reaches beyond adding an occurrence hook and makes the registered metric-alert handler abstract, so `group_type.detector_handler(self)` raises `TypeError` whenever a `metric_alert_fire` detector is processed because it implements none of `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or `build_occurrence_and_event_data`.

src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:128 — P1 [anchor:100] Changing the base `evaluate` contract to `-> dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` is unneeded scope expansion beyond the occurrence hook and breaks every unmodified list-returning `DetectorHandler` integration, because `process_detectors` now unconditionally calls `detector_results.values()` at line 60 and a legacy list has no `values` method.

P1 src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:299 — The newly introduced `result, event_data = self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` publishes alert occurrences whose only available detector project is the hard-coded `return 1`, so a detector in any organization emits data into project 1 and exposes/corrupts that tenant's issue stream.

tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:190 — P2 [anchor:75] `detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH` supplies 6 for a packet whose `group_2` value is 10, while `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` discards `value`; this test therefore passes if the new occurrence hook is called with the wrong evaluated value for every group and fails to verify that the changed `build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, ...)` contract preserves that value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — Every `metric_alert_fire` detector now fails with `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler` because `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):\n    pass` inherits the unimplemented abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` methods, so `detector_handler` cannot be created and no packet is processed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows MetricAlertDetectorHandler changing from extending DetectorHandler with a concrete evaluate() method to extending StatefulDetectorHandler with just 'pass'. Looking at StatefulDetectorHandler in the diff, it has multiple @abc.abstractmethod decorators: get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). The test file shows MockDetectorStateHandler implementing these methods (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data). Since MetricAlertDetectorHandler only has 'pass' and doesn't implement these abstract methods, attempting to instantiate it will raise TypeError. This is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — P1 [anchor:100] Replacing the working placeholder with `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass` reaches beyond adding an occurrence hook and makes the registered metric-alert handler abstract, so `group_type.detector_handler(self)` raises `TypeError` whenever a `metric_alert_fire` detector is processed because it implements none of `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or `build_occurrence_and_event_data`.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that MetricAlertDetectorHandler will raise TypeError because it doesn't implement abstract methods. However, looking at the diff, StatefulDetectorHandler defines abstract methods (get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, build_occurrence_and_event_data), but MetricAlertDetectorHandler with 'pass' is a valid subclass declaration. The class won't raise TypeError at instantiation time in Python unless you actually try to instantiate it AND call those abstract methods. The test file shows MockDetectorStateHandler properly implementing these methods for testing. The MetricAlertDetectorHandler is likely a placeholder that won't be instantiated in production yet (the TODO comment even says 'This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction'). The finding assumes this code path is actively used, but the diff doesn't show evidence of that.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:128 — P1 [anchor:100] Changing the base `evaluate` contract to `-> dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` is unneeded scope expansion beyond the occurrence hook and breaks every unmodified list-returning `DetectorHandler` integration, because `process_detectors` now unconditionally calls `detector_results.values()` at line 60 and a legacy list has no `values` method.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that changing the return type breaks 'every unmodified list-returning DetectorHandler integration'. However, looking at the diff, the abstract base class `DetectorHandler.evaluate` method signature is also changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` (line 125-127). All concrete implementations shown in the diff (`MockDetectorHandler`, `StatefulDetectorHandler`) are updated to return dicts. The `process_detectors` function at line 60 calls `.values()` on the result, which works correctly with the new dict return type. There's no evidence of any 'legacy list-returning' handlers that would break - all handlers in the codebase shown are updated consistently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1 src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:299 — The newly introduced `result, event_data = self.build_occurrence_and_event_data(...)` publishes alert occurrences whose only available detector project is the hard-coded `return 1`, so a detector in any organization emits data into project 1 and exposes/corrupts that tenant's issue stream.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that `project_id` property in `Detector` model (line 55-57 in detector.py model file) returns a hardcoded `return 1` with a comment 'XXX: Temporary property until we add `project_id` to the model.' The new code path at line 299-301 calls `self.build_occurrence_and_event_data()` which in the test implementation uses `handler.detector.project_id`. This means all detectors will emit occurrences with project_id=1 regardless of which organization/project they belong to, which is a real data isolation/security bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:190 — P2 [anchor:75] `detector.detector_handler, "group_2", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH` supplies 6 for a packet whose `group_2` value is 10, while `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` discards `value`; this test therefore passes if the new occurrence hook is called with the wrong evaluated value for every group and fails to verify that the changed `build_occurrence_and_event_data(group_key, value, ...)` contract preserves that value.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in the test at line 190, `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` is called with value=6 for group_2, but the data packet specifies `'group_2': 10`. Looking at the `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` function (lines 244-278), the `value` parameter is indeed not used in constructing the occurrence or event_data - it's just a parameter that gets ignored. This means the test doesn't actually verify that the correct value is passed through the `build_occurrence_and_event_data` contract. However, this is a test quality issue (missing verification of the value parameter), not a bug in the production code. The test would pass even if the wrong value was passed to `build_occurrence_and_event_data`.
